Bug_Title: NP: Null value is guaranteed to be dereferenced (NP_GUARANTEED_DEREF)
Bug_Details:
There is a statement or branch that if executed guarantees that
      a value is null at this point, and that
      value that is guaranteed to be dereferenced
      (except on forward paths involving runtime exceptions).
       Note that a check such as
    if (x == null) throw new NullPointerException();
    is treated as a dereference of x. if (x == null) throw new NullPointerException(); x
Bug_Explanation: The bug is embedded in the code by adding a null value to the list and then attempting to uppercase it with the toUpperCase() method. This will cause a NullPointerException to be thrown.
Trigger_Explanation: The test case adds three elements to a list, with the third element being null. The for-each loop iterates over the list and calls the toUpperCase() method on each element. Since the third element is null, this method call will trigger a NullPointerException and the test case will fail.
